purpose: Classify native data shared by two workspaces. A package download, a compiler artifact, or an in-memory program is never semantic-index reuse.

servers.reason: The TypeScript language service keeps its project program in the server process.
Pyright's analysis program is process-local; its package cache is not an index shared by projects.
Intelephense global storage is provider storage, but no stable cross-workspace semantic-index contract is exposed.
VS Code CSS language service builds stylesheet state in the server process.
bash-language-server has no documented persistent semantic index.
Roslyn project state is process-local; NuGet and SDK artifacts are dependency inputs, not shared solution indexes.

clangd may mount a separately built external index. The normal background index is workspace-local. The shipped 23.1.0 background-index probe resolved the common header but logged a fresh branch-B shard build, so it does not prove a cross-workspace cache hit.
JDT LS receives its own -data directory for every workspace.

The shipped Kotlin Language Server's native RocksDB index can share immutable library/project data. It needs a compatible JVM server runtime and a real imported Gradle/Maven project before an opt-in probe can assert records.
SharpRail creates and disposes an isolated IntelliJ system path for every workspace.
Ruby LSP does not expose a durable cross-workspace semantic-index contract.
gopls supports GOPLSCACHE, a content-addressed semantic cache shared by workspaces.
rust-analyzer's project graph and analysis database are workspace/session state; Cargo caches are dependency artifacts.
The shipped Metals 1.6.9 SqlSharedIndices may reuse the immutable JDK src.zip hierarchy. Coursier cache sharing only proves dependency artifacts and is excluded from semantic reuse.
languageserver does not expose a durable cross-workspace semantic-index contract.
PowerShell Editor Services keeps script analysis in its session; module downloads are not semantic indexes.
SourceKit-LSP indexes and build products belong to the package/build workspace.
Dart Analysis Server can use a supplied shared analysis cache. The opt-in probe supplies one identical cache path to both workspaces.
